answer: Every new identity must enter through a single narrow inlet that prices admission by congestion: the fee for the nth registration in an epoch rises with the square of n, and it can only be paid in seasoned timber — a non-transferable receipt that accrues solely by holding a stake untouched through a full epoch. One honest agent pays a small fee with one season of holding; an attacker minting a hundred clones at zephyr speed pays a hundredfold fee per clone, and no clone can borrow another's timber, so each fake identity costs its own full season.
